elements.element: Preferred alternative A: renewal only by mutual written agreement
elements.evidence: "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — renewal is automatic, not by mutual written agreement

elements.element: Preferred alternative B(i): automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date"

elements.element: Preferred alternative B(ii): Customer may opt out on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other" — either Party, so Customer may exit on 30 days' notice

elements.element: Preferred alternative B(iii): Vendor reminder notice 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic anywhere in the redlined clause; text ends at "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated"

elements.element: Preferred alternative B(iv): renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: Clause is silent on renewal pricing; no cap language inserted ("unless terminated by either Party hereto upon thirty (30) days written notice")
"shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period"

elements.element: Fallback (ii): non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other" — 30 days is within the 60-day ceiling
No price-increase right exists in the clause ("continue for a period of one (1) year"; renewal terms silent on price), so the condition for a cap is demonstrably absent

reasons: The single operation changes only the notice number from ninety to thirty days, which is the smallest possible edit and satisfies the fallback notice window; nothing unrelated was touched and no undefined term or dangling mechanic was introduced.

The locked target is preferred, but two preferred atomic elements are absent: there is no Vendor reminder obligation 60 days before renewal and no cap on renewal price increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%. The official precision check confirms the price-cap element must be stated even where the original is silent.

To reach the locked preferred level, add a concise sentence: Vendor shall notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each renewal, and any price increase on renewal shall not exceed the lesser of CPI and 3%.

The clause now sits at the fallback on its material terms (automatic renewal with a 30-day exit right available to Customer), so it is acceptable rather than walk-away; the official literal pattern failure for the notice window is a pattern-matching artefact — thirty (30) days is plainly within the 60-day ceiling.
Note the exit right is bilateral rather than a Customer-only opt-out; this does not disadvantage us relative to the original, which was also bilateral.
